writeup: TIC 468152519 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 5.2842 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing 1.93% dimming, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 54.4 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. A secondary eclipse was not detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates near the target location, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 14.5, though the centroid offset of 3.6 arcsec warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting a potentially novel object. The automated pipeline's machine learning screening assigned this system a score of 0.52, indicating moderate confidence in its stellar nature. The data passed all quality checks without flags.
